description:
Top-level `expected` keys that are DATA under test, not assertion names, so no driver names them as a literal. Each entry needs a reason. check_expected_keys_read.py reports an entry as STALE once a driver does read the key, so a real assertion landing here surfaces its own cleanup rather than leaving a permanent exemption.

Two entries were removed once the checker learned to recognise a driver that iterates or deep-equals the WHOLE `expected` map — the well-written form, which names no key and so read as asserting nothing. `sensitive_keys_default.json` and `redaction_config.json` were exempted for exactly that reason, which is now detected rather than allowlisted (sync finding B-004).

allow.reason: 403 / 202 for the approval outcomes. NO SDK exposes a code-to-HTTP mapping — `grep -ri http_status` across apcore-python, apcore-typescript and apcore-rust `src/` returns nothing. The mapping lives in the transport adapters (express-apcore, fastapi-apcore), which are separate repos with their own conformance surface. There is nothing on the thrown error for a core-SDK driver to observe, and restating 403 from the fixture would assert nothing. The drivers assert `error_code` instead, which is the core-SDK-observable half of the same contract.
allow.removable_when: the transport adapters gain a conformance driver against this fixture, or the core SDKs grow a code-to-HTTP mapping
